summary:
ARES Jezero: Tactical EVA Autonav & Mars Surface Telemetry Platform
Team Stella developed ARES Jezero, a mission-critical 3D surface operations and tactical EVA telemetry platform engineered for astronaut traverses and rover autonav across the Jezero Crater Western Delta.

The system addresses NASA's challenge by fusing five authentic planetary datasets into an operational decision framework: USGS MOLA/HiRISE digital elevation models (10m grid), THEMIS thermal inertia loose sand hazards (<150 TIU), CRISM/PIXL mineralogy, MSL RAD topographic radiation shielding, and real-time NASA MEDA atmospheric telemetry. A kinematically constrained A* graph search computes viable paths across three specialized operational modes: Habitat Mission Console, Glove-Ready EVA Field Slate (with Apollo walkback envelopes and metabolic O₂ burn tracking), and an immersive 1.8m eye-level Helmet Visor HUD. It also streams real Perseverance camera captures (Hazcam, Mastcam-Z, Navcam, and animated convective dust vortices).

This tool is critical because it bridges the gap between raw orbital science and human astronaut survival on Mars, transforming static reconnaissance data into mathematically verified, kinematically viable navigation corridors for human exploration of the Red Planet.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Ares Jezero (ARES-OCTANT) is an aerospace-grade tactical 3D GIS and extravehicular activity (EVA) navigation platform designed for human exploration of Jezero Crater, Mars. Because the 4 to 22-minute light-time communication latency to Earth prevents real-time tactical assistance from Mission Control, surface crews must make safety-critical routing and life-support decisions autonomously.

Our platform operates across three tailored operational environments:

1. Habitat Mission Console: A desktop workstation for flight controllers featuring dockable telemetry panels, active waypoint inspection, NASA MEDA atmospheric weather monitoring, and an interactive Google Earth-style 3D Mars globe with atmospheric limb scattering, deep-space starfields, and real-time orbital tracking of MRO, Phobos, and Deimos.

2. Astronaut Field Slate (Tablet): A forearm-mounted touch interface built to NASA-STD-3001 ergonomics. It features 48px glove-friendly touch targets, left/right-hand docking, high-glare polarized solar filtration, and a Portable Life Support System (PLSS) monitor tracking oxygen consumption, suit pressure (4.28 psi O₂), metabolic heat dissipation, and titanium sample core logging.

3. Helmet Visor AR HUD: An eye-level (1.8m) heads-up display projecting a 360° conformal compass tape, waypoint locking reticles, and EVA abort vectors directly into the astronaut’s field of view.

Our routing engine uses an A* pathfinder integrated with the Minetti bio-kinetic cost-of-transport model. Rather than calculating simple Euclidean distance, it factors in astronaut mass (140 kg with PLSS in 0.38g), slope-dependent metabolic oxygen burn rates, and dynamically steers routes away from steep loose scree (>15°) and dangerous low-thermal-inertia sand drift pockets

Benefits & Intended Impact

Ares Jezero bridges the gap between planetary science and frontline operational safety:

- Autonomous EVA Safety: Real-time Walkback Safety Limit calculation ensures that unassisted foot travel never exceeds primary oxygen margins (guaranteeing the mandatory 30-minute reserve per EVA-FR-101).

- Crew Proximity & Comms Tracking: Proximity radar warns if crew buddy separation exceeds 100 meters (EVA-FR-102), while line-of-sight tracking predicts orbital UHF relay passes through the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO).

- Mission Impact: Proves how orbital datasets can be transformed into actionable, life-critical surface navigation tools for future Moon-to-Mars crewed architectures.


Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Languages: TypeScript, JavaScript, GLSL (OpenGL Shading Language), HTML5, CSS3.

- Frameworks & Libraries: React 19, Three.js (WebGL 3D graphics), Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons.

- Build & Deployment: Vite 8, Rolldown / OXC build tooling, deployed live on Vercel with single-page application routing.

- Avionics Audio: Native Web Audio API procedural synthesizer for telemetry chimes, proximity pings, and comms alerts (100% code-synthesized with zero external media files).

- NASA Datasets: USGS MOLA / HiRISE Jezero Digital Elevation Models, official NASA Mars Trek 3D surface meshes (323K STL and 970K OBJ photogrammetry), MRO CTX optical mosaics, and Mars 2020 Perseverance MEDA atmospheric weather telemetry.

Creativity & Key Design Factors

Our design was driven by the extreme physical constraints of Mars:

- Physical Spacesuit Ergonomics: Standard interfaces fail when dexterity drops 70% in pressurized gloves and harsh Martian sun washes out displays. We designed high-contrast color palettes, large target paddings, and forearm-docked layouts.

- Continuous Multi-Scale Exploration: Astronauts can zoom seamlessly from interplanetary orbital vantage points (Google Earth-style globe with atmospheric Fresnel scattering) down to 1.8-meter first-person eye-level terrain navigation.

- Scientific Fidelity: We integrated authentic multi-spectral orbital GIS layers—CRISM aqueous clays/carbonates, THEMIS thermal sand hazard maps, RAD radiation topographic shielding, and continuous elevation contour lines—giving crew members immediate situational awareness of both geological targets and surface hazards.


2. Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

Super Intelligence (SI) and AI development tools were utilized during this project strictly for software engineering acceleration, code optimization, and scientific formula implementation:

- Code and Data:

Large Language Model (LLM) tools were used to assist with frontend component scaffolding, TypeScript type definitions, translation of the scientific Minetti (2002) metabolic energy expenditure polynomial into algorithmic TypeScript, and formulating the GLSL shaders for atmospheric Fresnel limb scattering and multi-spectral terrain layer blending. All underlying scientific datasets (elevation grids, rover imagery, mineralogical bands, and atmospheric readings) are sourced directly from public-domain NASA, USGS, and JPL mission archives.

- Audio:

All tactical avionics audio cues, radio clicks, and interface feedback alerts were programmatically synthesized via code using the browser’s native Web Audio API (procedural oscillators and gain envelopes). AI tools assisted in calculating the harmonic frequency intervals (sine and square wave combinations) used in the synthesizer script. No third-party or AI-generated external audio files were used.

- Images and Videos:

All surface textures, elevation maps, and photogrammetry models are derived directly from official NASA MRO Context Camera (CTX), HiRISE, and Mars Trek archives. No AI text-to-image foundation models were used to generate or alter rover photography, surface maps, or planetary bodies. No NASA logos, flags, or protected agency insignias were generated or modified by AI.
